title: Arkret Realm Link Self-Management Operation DTOs
description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface cross-Realm link operations (ak.self.realm_link.*). Each write carries the caller-signed ak.realm.link Move and the service submits those exact bytes through ordinary Event admission, so the reducer still validates self-reference, link kind and the FSM transition. General link-graph cycles are legal; traversal uses a visited set and does not reject a write merely for forming a cycle. The durable link payload is the canonical ak.realm.link; see spec/v1/zh/models/realm-links.md.

link_kind.description: Core value or machine-registered extension kind using x.<reverse-dns>.<name>; unregistered extension values fail closed.

commitment.description: Optional opaque commitment / proof reference linking this edge to an external attestation.

realm_link_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for both cross-Realm link writes. Create and tombstone are the same Event kind writing the same (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) FSM cell, so they share one submission def and differ only in the status their payload names. Edge fields MUST be carried inside the caller-signed Event; accepting them directly for a service-added signature is forbidden by capabilities.md sections 118/361 and key-management.md section 411. The source Realm is single-sourced by event.realm_id and MUST equal the path realm_id; the rest of the edge is event.payload (realm_link_payload). The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller, and rejects self-reference with schema_violation + realm_link_self_reference and an illegal FSM transition with failed_precondition + realm_link_invalid_transition. Because the payload names the status the edge is moving to, a concurrent write on the same triple makes the later submission fail its transition check rather than silently overwriting.

realm_link_create_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.link Move and nothing else. target_realm_id, link_kind, status and the optional label / commitment all live in link_event.event.payload.

link_event.description: Closed ak.realm.link Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_link_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed tombstoning ak.realm.link Move and nothing else. The edge is single-sourced by link_event.event.payload: target_realm_id MUST equal the path target_realm_id, and link_kind is named there rather than in a query parameter, because a query parameter is outside the bytes the caller signs. Deleting an edge is the same durable Event kind as creating one -- every peer has to converge on the removal too -- so this operation keeps its event_log effect.

link_event.description: Closed ak.realm.link Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with payload.status pinned to tombstoned.

realm_effective_policy_outcome.description: Merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy declaration.

inheritance_mode.description: explicit when the Realm has projected a ak.realm.inheritance_policy; none otherwise (implicit inheritance is forbidden).
